keyVerseText: The LORD is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God, and I will prepare him an habitation; my father's God, and I will exalt him.
rootMeaning: The word יָהּ (Yâhh) is a contracted form of the divine name יְהֹוָה (Yᵉhôvâh), which means 'the existing One.' This contraction preserves the sacredness and uniqueness of God's name while providing a shorter, poetic form used especially in worship contexts. The root meaning emphasizes God's eternal and self-existent nature, which goes beyond the common English gloss 'the LORD' by highlighting His unchanging and sovereign existence.
usageInScripture: יָהּ appears 48 times in the Hebrew Bible, predominantly in poetic and liturgical passages such as the Psalms and early Hebrew poems. It is often translated simply as 'the LORD' or 'Jah,' reflecting its function as a sacred, reverent name for God. The consistency in translation underscores its role as a proper name for the one true God, used especially to invoke His power, presence, and praise within worship settings.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יָהּ as a contracted form of the divine name יְהֹוָה deepens our appreciation for God's self-existence and eternal nature, foundational truths for Christian faith. This name reveals God's unchanging character and His intimate involvement with His people, as seen in worship and praise. Recognizing יָהּ as the sacred and vehement name of God invites believers to respond with reverence and trust in His sovereign power, which is ultimately fulfilled in the person of Jesus Christ, who reveals God to us fully. The use of this name in Scripture affirms the continuity of God's identity from the Old Testament covenant to the New Testament revelation.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 15:2 declares, 'The LORD is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation.' Here, the use of יָהּ as 'the LORD' emphasizes God's powerful and saving presence. This name conveys not only God's identity but also His active role as protector and deliverer. The verse calls believers to recognize God as their personal source of strength and salvation, highlighting the intimate relationship between the worshipper and the eternal, self-existent God revealed in this sacred name.
